status: CLOSED. Four PRs open, none merged, none deployed. Three of four CI states are as good as they can be before a merge; the fourth is red for two reasons, one of which clears on the dashboards merge and one of which this lane did not cause and did not absorb. The token landed as one identical blob in four repos, the stranded workaround was proven to fire and was retired in the open, and the two-renderings question turned out to be stale by one merge - with a real, different divergence found underneath it and routed rather than settled.
missionPremise: `--sc-ok` `#2F7A52` on `--sc-ok-wash` `#E3F0E8` computes 4.444:1 against the 4.5:1 floor that applies to normal text. Both are tokens in `web/sc-kit.css`, a file whose own header states it is byte-identical across `smartcity-dashboards`, `smart-files` and `plan-review` and that a repo which edits a token value has forked the system - so the fix cannot be a Dashboards PR, it has to land as identical bytes in three product repos plus the kit's vendored copy. The row is urgent rather than tidy because G-97 R3, unable to use the failing pill, rendered a resolved status quiet instead and DELIBERATELY wrote a test that computes the ratio live and fails once the kit is fixed, so landing the token alone turns main red on purpose. Sources: OPS-17 amendment A-082, taken 2026-08-19 on the operator's ruling 'fan agents to do that'; `_decisions/2026-08-17_smartcity_product_line_design_system.md` (one Empressa kit governs Dashboards, Smart Files, Plan Review and future Asset Management); `_decisions/2026-08-17_smartcity_visual_law.md` (quiet surfaces, loud exceptions, honest absence; inverted applicability - a pass is quiet; light is first-class); and the four-PR cross-repo shape established by `_inbox/2026-08-19_g94_close.json`.
completionPredicate: A stranger can evaluate this without me by doing six things. (1) `git ls-tree g98/sc-ok-contrast web/sc-kit.css` in all three product repos and `vendor/sc-kit.css` in the kit returns ONE blob hash, `3b89d4ae402dc974092950f1bbdcc1e5a96fbf7a`. (2) `git diff main...g98/sc-ok-contrast -- web/sc-kit.css` in each product repo shows exactly ONE changed line, and it is a token VALUE; no token added, renamed or removed, no rule and no selector touched, and `web/index.html` untouched in all four repos. (3) Restoring `main`'s `src/render-lenses.test.mjs` over the branch and running `node --test src/render-lenses.test.mjs` fails with 'the light p-ok pair is now 4.62:1 and passes AA', proving the strand fired for the real reason rather than being narrated as having fired. (4) Running `P:/tmp/k1-scan/probe.mjs` against the branch reports 4 failing groups where the base reported 5, the removed one being `pill.p-ok`, over the same 186,528-row denominator. (5) Every ratio quoted anywhere in this close travels with its counting rule. (6) The one kit CI failure is reproducible on pristine `main`-vs-`main`, proving it inherited rather than caused.
scopeBasis: The boundaries are drawn where the work stops being a token value. IN: the one `--sc-ok` light declaration every failing element resolves to, in all three product repos plus the kit's vendored copy; the kit gate whose pinned delta a value change necessarily moves; and the three comments plus one live assertion in `smartcity-dashboards` that were written ON the defect and become false when it is fixed. OUT, deliberately, each for a named reason. (a) The dark `--sc-ok`: measured at 6.171:1 as rendered and 5.068:1 at its theoretical worst; a change with no defect behind it is not a fix. (b) `--sc-ok-wash` in either theme: it is a separate token and it is the background this fix is measured against, so moving it changes what the fix is measured against - the same reasoning G-94 recorded for `--sc-quiet-wash`. (c) `web/index.html` in every repo: G-100 owns three line ranges there. (d) `scripts/a11y-scan.mjs`, `src/a11y-gate*`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: G-99 owns them, including the adjudication this lane's largest finding argues against. (e) The `.sep` contrast defect (1.737:1, larger than the one this row is about): it is a token-CONSUMER question and its fix is markup in a file G-100 owns. (f) The `inspected`-axis rendering divergence: `inspected` is true for `failed` too, so quieting on it would quiet a failed inspection; the correct generalisation is a rule change and DEV_PROCESS 5.4 says propose. (g) Re-vendoring the kit's `index.html`, `app.js` and `shell.css`: pulls markup requiring the `Prov` component to accept two source segments, a component-contract change; declined by G-94 for that reason and again here for the same one. (h) Reconciling doc_repo `30b_smartcity_design_system.md`/.html section 4.1, which still declares the pre-G-94 AND pre-G-98 values: editing a canonical doc is planner-owned. (i) Any scan of the `smart-files` or `plan-review` surfaces: those repos received identical bytes because the token block is identical, not because their surfaces were measured, and their PRs say so.

domProbe.instrument: P:/tmp/k1-scan/probe.mjs. Serves this repo's own src/server.mjs on an EPHEMERAL port, drives real Chromium via playwright-core, seeds the localStorage theme lever through addInitScript and ASSERTS document.documentElement's data-theme equals the requested theme before reading - an unapplied theme throws rather than being reported as a scanned theme (the G-94 F-A shape, carried forward). For every element with a direct non-empty text child it reads the computed colour and walks ancestors compositing every non-transparent background layer source-over until an opaque one is reached, then chooses the 4.5 or 3.0 threshold from the RENDERED size and weight.

theRealRemainingDivergence.disposition: ROUTED WITH A RECOMMENDATION, deliberately not changed, so a successor can tell a deliberate exclusion from an oversight.
reasons: It is a DIFFERENT AXIS, not the same divergence. `inspected` is true for failed and corrections as well as passed, so mapping `inspected` to quiet would quiet a FAILED inspection. The correct generalisation is one satisfied-band predicate across both vocabularies - identifiable as severity === 'ok' in each - and that is a RULE change, not a value change.

It changes what a demo screen renders, on a renderer that merged hours before this lane started, against a visual-law clause the operator ratified in prose but that nobody has yet applied to the result axis. DEV_PROCESS 5.4: propose, do not unilaterally remediate.

Against this lane's own interest, and said for that reason: if `passed` were quieted too, p-ok would become UNREACHABLE in smartcity-dashboards and this lane's own token fix would have no live consumer left on this product to verify against.

findings.title: The largest measured contrast defect on this product is NOT --sc-ok. It is the .sep separator glyph, at 1.737:1 - and an adjudication is currently hiding it.
findings.measured: web/shell.css:179 `.prov .sep { color: var(--sc-line-strong); }` paints a `|` character on the .prov chip's own ground. Light #AEBAC5 on --sc-surface-2 #F6F8FA = 1.855:1; dark #3B4854 on #18212A = 1.737:1. 874 element rows per theme across all 23 surfaces, 167 of them in viewport, plus a further 46 per theme on a white/surface ground. There are 17 `class="sep"` occurrences in web/index.html.
findings.whyNobodyHasSeenIt: axe files that region as INCOMPLETE with reason elmPartiallyObscuring rather than as a violation, because .nav-foot is position:sticky with an opaque background and axe will not composite through an overlap. src/a11y-gate.mjs REVIEW_ITEMS[0] then adjudicates it at a ceiling of 1 node per theme.
findings.correctionOwed: the adjudication reasons, quoted at source from src/a11y-gate.mjs:145: 'SUPPORTS. web/shell.css gives .nav-foot position: sticky with an OPAQUE background (var(--sc-surface)), so the nav list scrolls underneath it and a person reads the footer text against a solid ground.' For the .sep children specifically that is refuted by direct computation: AGAINST the solid ground, at the declared token values, the glyph is 1.855:1 in light and 1.737:1 in dark. The adjudication may well be right about the region's other children; it is wrong about these, and 'a person reads it against a solid ground' is not an argument that the colour is legible.
findings.disposition: OUT OF SCOPE, routed. src/a11y-gate.mjs is G-99's file by dispatch and the markup is G-100's.
findings.recommendedFix: aria-hidden="true" on the .sep spans. A `|` between two data items is pure decoration, WCAG 1.4.3 exempts decoration, and hiding it REMOVES the nodes rather than recolouring them - which is better than raising --sc-line-strong, a token whose job is faint hairlines.

findings.handling: the kit's gate 1c was widened in BOTH directions as EXACT line arrays, not filters, so a new divergence still turns it red; the injection harness confirms gate 1c still fires. vendor/30b-section-4.1.css was NOT hand-edited, because that would make the kit assert a doc_repo state doc_repo does not have.
findings.owed: planner-owned edit to 30b section 4.1 in both .md and .html, after which the kit re-vendors the extract and gate 1c narrows back to one line.

findings.title: Nothing still asserts the cross-repo byte identity the design system depends on.
findings.detail: G-94 measured this as F-B and it is unchanged: one of three edges is checked, one-directionally, by the kit's vendor-parity. smart-files and plan-review could drift from dashboards indefinitely and every CI in the program would stay green. This lane relied on the same manual procedure G-94 did - pipe the bytes, verify the blob hash - which works and is not a control.
findings.recommendation: one card: a check comparing the three product copies against each other, plus CI for plan-review, which has none at all.

findings.title: A hypothetical pair sweep produced three dark failures that do not exist, and the DOM probe is why that was caught.
findings.detail: compositing every wash over every surface token gave dark crit 4.445, restricted 4.406 and quiet 3.953 - all of them only over --sc-surface-3, which web/shell.css uses on :hover states. A hover state is not a rendered state and axe does not scan one. The same sweep also flagged light --sc-atom on --sc-atom-wash at 4.166:1, which never fails because web/shell.css declares no .p-atom rule and nothing pairs those two tokens as text-on-wash.
findings.bearing: a coverage figure travels with its denominator (DEV_PROCESS 1.1). Three of these would have been reported as defects on a denominator no element occupies. Recorded because the discard is part of the record, not because the numbers matter.

findings.title: A foreign SmartCity Dashboards server is listening on port 8791 and was NOT touched.
findings.measured: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:8791/` returns 200 and the body's <title> is 'SmartCity Dashboards'. Every server this lane started bound an EPHEMERAL port via `server.listen(0)`; the two it used, 59438 and 64830, both probe http_code=000 (connection refused) after the runs, which is how the kills were verified - by probing the port, not by trusting a pid.
findings.disposition: not this lane's process and not killed. The contract forbids a blanket kill over node processes because other lanes are running on this machine; reported so the planner can decide, not acted on.

constraintsHonored: token VALUES only: one declaration line in sc-kit.css. No token added, renamed or removed; no rule, no selector, no wash, no type ramp, no geometry, no spacing, no duration.
both themes measured; dark was measured, found compliant at 6.171:1 as rendered, and deliberately NOT moved, with the measurement stated rather than the omission implied.
every ratio quoted with its counting rule at the point of use, and truncated rather than rounded.
proof taken at a TALL viewport as well as the default - 1440x3000 alongside 1440x900 - and the viewport-boundedness figure reported (7 of 308 in view).

web/index.html untouched in all four repos; scripts/a11y-scan.mjs, src/a11y-gate* and .github/workflows/ci.yml untouched. Verified by `git diff --name-only main...branch` per repo, not by recollection.
P:/tmp/k2-dash and P:/tmp/k3-dash never created, never entered, never read. No sibling lane's clone or process touched.
NO broad kill over node processes. The foreign server on 8791 was identified read-only and left alone.

all verification EXIT-BOUNDED: git and gh one-shots, node --test, npm test, and probes that bind an ephemeral port and close the server in a finally block. Kills verified by probing the port (http_code=000), never by trusting a pid.
no merge, no deploy. Deploys are planner-owned and CODE-DONE is not CUSTOMER-DONE: none of this is on a serving revision.
live Bastrop not touched and not read. No feed connected. G-52 not started. G-24 not filled. L26 untouched.
no sub-agents spawned; this lane was the deepest worker as instructed.
doc_repo edits left UNCOMMITTED: only the three artifacts the dispatch named were written.

instruments: P:/tmp/k1-scan/contrast.mjs - WCAG ratio maths, source-over sRGB compositing, HSL conversion, truncating formatters
P:/tmp/k1-scan/measure.mjs - the target pair in both themes over every surface composite
P:/tmp/k1-scan/allpairs.mjs - the hypothetical pair sweep, kept because discarding it is part of the record (finding K1-F-H)
P:/tmp/k1-scan/choose.mjs - the HSL-ray walk behind the value choice
P:/tmp/k1-scan/probe.mjs - the DOM measurement, 23 surfaces x 2 themes x 2 viewports, with a theme-lever assertion that throws rather than reporting an unapplied theme as scanned
P:/tmp/k1-scan/where-pok.mjs - locates the rendered p-ok elements
P:/tmp/k1-scan/refresh-one.mjs - a targeted re-vendor mirroring scripts/refresh-vendor.mjs's logic for a named subset, so the manifest is still written by a program rather than by hand in two places
P:/tmp/k1-scan/probe-before.json, probe-after.json, a11y-main.log, a11y-branch.log, probe-after.log - raw results

note: these live in P:/tmp scratch. Per DEV_PROCESS 6.1 a guardrail that does not survive a clone is not a guardrail; none of this is proposed as a gate, and if any of it should become one - the DOM probe is the obvious candidate for G-99, since it is viewport-independent by construction - it has to move into a repo first.
